cards.text: Last time, the LORD scattered people from Babel over the face of all the earth. Now Genesis follows one family line, the account of Shem, Noah’s son. Two years after the flood, when Shem is 100, he becomes the father of Arphaxad.

Then it’s son after son: Shelah, Eber, Peleg, Reu, Serug, and Nahor, who becomes the father of Terah. Each man has his son, lives on for years, and has other sons and daughters. Shem lives 500 more years after Arphaxad is born, and by the time we get to Nahor it’s 119, which, friend, is the SHORT one!
When Terah is 70, he becomes the father of Abram, Nahor and Haran. Yes, ANOTHER Nahor, so somebody yells “NAHOR!” at the family reunion and two heads turn.

cards.question: Terah’s son Haran has a son of his own. What’s his name?

cards.text: Then hard news. Haran dies in his native land, Ur of the Chaldeans.

cards.question: True or false: Haran dies while his father Terah is still alive.

cards.text: I bet that one hurts Terah, saying goodbye to his own son. Then Abram marries Sarai, and Nahor marries Milcah.

cards.question: Nahor’s wife Milcah is the daughter of ___.
Genesis has listed sons and daughters for man after man. True or false: Abram and Sarai have children too.

cards.text: After that long list of babies, this one lands heavy: Sarai is barren. Then Terah takes Abram and Sarai and sets out from Ur of the Chaldeans for the land of Canaan.

cards.question: Lot’s father Haran has died. True or false: Terah brings his grandson Lot along on the trip.
Terah’s family is headed for Canaan. But where do they stop and settle?

cards.text: Haran. The town, not the son. They head out for Canaan and settle on the way, like starting a cross-country road trip and moving into a rest stop for good.

cards.question: Terah lives ___ years, and he dies in ___.

cards.text: Then the LORD speaks to Abram, and it’s a BIG ask. Leave your country, your kindred, and your father’s household.

cards.question: God tells Abram to leave it all behind. Where is Abram supposed to go?

answers.text: To a land God will show him
Back to Ur of the Chaldeans
Down to the land of Egypt

cards.text: No name, no map, no address. That’s like your boss saying, “Pack up your whole life. I’ll text you the address later.”

cards.question: Sarai has no children. But what does God promise to make Abram into?

cards.text: Remember the builders at Babel, who wanted to make a name for themselves? Now listen to what God promises Abram.

cards.question: God says, “I will bless you; I will make your ___ great.”
God promises to bless Abram. True or false: God says that blessing is meant for Abram alone.

cards.text: God keeps going. He will bless those who bless Abram and curse those who curse him, and then comes the last line. Lean in, friend.

cards.question: Who does God say will be blessed through Abram?

answers.text: All the families of the earth

cards.question: God has made Abram huge promises and still hasn’t named the land. True or false: Abram goes, just as the LORD told him.
Abram is ___ years old when he leaves Haran.

cards.text: Seventy-five! I spent years in a junk drawer doing NOTHING, and this man packs up Sarai, his nephew Lot, and all the possessions and people they’d gathered in Haran, and sets out for Canaan.

cards.question: Terah’s trip stopped in Haran. True or false: this time, Abram makes it all the way to the land of Canaan.

cards.text: He MAKES it, friend! Abram travels through the land as far as the Oak of Moreh at Shechem.

cards.question: True or false: when Abram gets there, the land of Canaan is empty, with nobody else living in it.

cards.text: The Canaanites are already in the land, so it’s like that boss finally texts the address and you walk in to find every desk taken. Then the LORD appears to Abram with a promise about this land.

cards.question: The LORD makes Abram a promise about this land. Who does He say He’ll give it to?
Right there, Abram builds something to the LORD, who appeared to him. What is it?
From there, Abram moves to the hill country east of Bethel, with Bethel to the west and Ai to the east. He pitches his ___ and builds another ___ to the LORD.

cards.text: There he calls on the name of the LORD, and then he journeys on toward the Negev. And that’s where we’ll leave Abram for now, friend, because trust me, this man’s road is just getting started.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 6 quotes "I will bless you; I will make your ___ great.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The opening card states two Bible facts from outside the passage without a reference: the LORD scattering people from Babel over the face of all the earth (Genesis 11:9) and Shem being Noah's son (Genesis 5:32). The card cites only Genesis 11:10, so the reference does not cover what the card tells.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: "Last time" treats the Babel passage as an earlier lesson the baker has already done. This is passage 1 of a new story group, and the passage before it is given only for context. Papa Dorin also can't know what the baker has done before.

rule.text: The passage right before it is also provided, for context only. It is not part of the lesson.

findings.problem: This story card tells only Genesis 11:4, which is outside the passage. It doesn't carry any part of Genesis 12 forward. It works as a callback, but its setup (Babel's builders wanting a name) never came earlier in this lesson. It also links Babel's name to Abram's name, a connection the texts never state.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: "Remember the builders at Babel, who wanted to make a name for themselves? Now listen to what God promises Abram" gives away the answer to the next card (card 6), whose blank is "name".

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The wrong answers "Every family living in Canaan" and "Every family living in Haran" are part of the right answer, "All the families of the earth" (Genesis 12:3). The families of Canaan and Haran are among the families of the earth, so a baker could argue either wrong answer is true.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.
